claims.claim: The layout is responsive by default with no media queries
claims.evidence: The component uses .wa-grid with --min-item-size, which relies on CSS auto-fill and minmax(). No @media queries appear anywhere in the output.

claims.claim: Card slots use slot='header' for styled header sections

claims.claim: Four metric cards fit side-by-side on desktop at 220px minimum
claims.evidence: Plausible but not verified. 4 x 220px = 880px plus gaps. Whether this fits depends on container width and gap values, which are not shown.

suggestions.assertion: Uses .wa-grid with --min-column-size for the metric cards row
suggestions.reason: The correct WA CSS custom property name should be verified against the actual Web Awesome API. The response used --min-item-size. If --min-item-size is the real WA property and --min-column-size is not, this assertion would unfairly penalize correct answers. Conversely, if --min-column-size is correct, the assertion is working as intended by catching the wrong property name.

No assertion checks whether the component actually imports from a Kigumi path (e.g., @/components/ui). The response does this correctly, but a raw HTML approach that mentions Card in text without an actual React import would also pass all current assertions.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cover the key layout patterns well. The --min-column-size vs --min-item-size discrepancy is the main point worth investigating to ensure the assertion tests the right property name.
